clue.text: Resentment of English earl during exhausting binges

parts.note: exhausting work is hard work

indicators.note: during places the two abbreviations within the word for binges, as if happening in their midst

parts.note: flings are bouts of wild indulgence, binges
E is an abbreviation for earl in peerage lists

explanation.surface: An English nobleman is resented for being present while others wear themselves out partying.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering bitterness after a dispute is resentment; the phrase is an everyday idiom for it.

indicators.note: created suggests the letters of the name are made into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A woman named Tabitha built her own surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural home or surroundings of an animal or person is an environment, a close synonym.

clue.text: Artist to pursue struggle for survival

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised artist
to trace someone is to track or follow them down

explanation.surface: A painter chases a living in a desperate competitive scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the relentless competitive grind of modern working life, a struggle to survive.

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters of the two names are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Two people, Flora and Dean, organised a dance together.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Provençal chain dance in which dancers hold hands, so an example of a dance.

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
to have contracted an illness is to have got it

explanation.surface: The monarch has caught an illness caused by a fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus attacking rye and other cereals, causing a plant disease and poisoning in people who eat it.

clue.text: Scotsman protects princess from the Middle East

indicators.note: protects suggests the man's name wraps round and shelters the princess

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
a rani is an Indian princess or queen

explanation.surface: A Scottish man guards a royal lady visiting from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Iran comes from the Middle East; the adjective fits the phrase.

indicators.note: away says the abbreviation for runs leaves the word for resentment

parts.note: resentment, the answer to 1 across, is a grudge
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
on can mean over, as in a lid on a box

explanation.surface: Bitterness disappears over a catch of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 across cross-reference needs a synonym, not the full phrase; 'runs' is cricket shorthand, and 'away' tells you it disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater fish of the carp family, used as bait, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: Stupid reason to test ancient artifact

indicators.note: stupid suggests the words are made senseless, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone finds it foolish to put logic to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: The inscribed Egyptian stone slab that unlocked hieroglyphs is a famous ancient artifact in the British Museum.

indicators.note: docking means cutting off, as with a tail, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an arbiter has control over a dispute or decision

explanation.surface: An elderly overseer is joining up with a satellite in orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking' looks like a spacecraft linking up, but it means cutting off: A is cut from ARBITER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft that circles a planet is a satellite.

parts.note: grand means splendid or wonderful
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A father's excellent advancement at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is an informal term for a man, and grandad is a familiar word for an elderly man or grandfather.

clue.text: Hearing several trapped in ruin, editor is crestfallen

indicators.note: trapped in places the hearing and number pieces between the word for ruin and the abbreviation

parts.note: to dish is to ruin, as in dishing someone's chances
an ear is the faculty of hearing
ten serves as an example of several

explanation.surface: An editor is dismayed on learning that people are trapped in a collapsed building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing several' sounds like news of victims, but it supplies two short words; 'trapped in' puts them between the ruin word and the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disheartened is to have lost spirit, the same as being crestfallen.

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
a train is a retinue of followers

explanation.surface: An entourage points out how to board a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to get on a train, that is to board it.

clue.text: Stumbles outside church — stretches out an arm

indicators.note: outside means the word for stumbles goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: trips means stumbles
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone trips just outside a church and flings out an arm to stop the fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm extends the elbow, so it stretches the arm out.

clue.text: It is returned by the tenth

indicators.note: is returned means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An item is sent back with a tenth of its value.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the Church.

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for artillery

parts.note: ordnance means military guns and artillery
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single order given within the artillery regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative order or decree, a command.

parts.note: inner can mean hidden or private, as in inner feelings
set means fixed or established, as in set ways

explanation.surface: A girl hid the old-fashioned china.
explanation.definitionFit: A matched set of plates and dishes for a meal is crockery.

clue.text: Quite a few noticed bagging game

indicators.note: bagging means putting something in a bag, so one word holds the other

parts.note: seen means noticed
an event is a sporting fixture or game

explanation.surface: A number of people spotted someone winning a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a fair number, so quite a few, a loose definition by example.

clue.text: State representative's passion for seductive woman

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
ire is anger, a fierce passion

explanation.surface: A politician has a passionate interest in an alluring woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp, a woman who seduces and exploits men, is called this; a seductress.

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A fresh mountain route shows promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just beginning to develop, so it has potential rather than full existence.

clue.text: His music's simple harmonies give away composer

indicators.note: give away means the words reveal letters concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Plain harmonies in a piece betray who wrote it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His music's' is part of the surface picture; the hidden run spans 'simple harmonies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow.

indicators.note: infiltrating means one piece gets inside the other

parts.note: le is French for the
Attic is the Greek of Athens

explanation.surface: A Greek agent penetrates the French spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework, a network of strips.

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone injects a dodgy drug in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively popular nightclub or venue is called this informally.

clue.text: The universe is losing carbon by diffusion

indicators.note: losing means the carbon symbol is dropped

parts.note: the cosmos is the universe
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
taken as written

explanation.surface: The universe is shedding carbon as it spreads out.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the diffusion of a solvent through a membrane.

indicators.note: accepts means the knight's title takes the other word inside

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A knight receives gratitude for playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.

indicators.note: into places the charity's letters inside the other piece
organisation suggests the letters are organised anew, rearranged

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Green campaigners are admitted to an exclusive group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' makes ETILE from 'elite'; NT goes in after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give a right to, to allow.

clue.text: Celebrated wealth being invested in hospital department

indicators.note: being invested in means the wealth word is placed inside the department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
a mine is a rich source, as in a mine of information or money

explanation.surface: A famous donor's money is put into a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent person is famous and respected, celebrated.

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone is noticed enjoying a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is a technique of painting in dots, so its result is spotted.

clue.text: Attend a soldier's party and make a run for it

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers
a treat is an outing or party

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a soldier's party and then flees.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a retreat is an idiom for leaving hastily, running away.
